title: Should Organic Food Be So Expensive?
summary: Business-news explainer on why organic food costs more: higher pest-control and labour costs, lower yields and certification fees, which push some small farms to drop certification while still farming organically.

assertions.quote: A pound of organic ground beef cost $14.99, about 80% more than a pound of regular ground beef.
Some small farms like this one used to be certified organic, but no longer are because they say they can't afford the certification fees

verdicts.note: Certification costs and paperwork lead some small growers to farm organically uncertified; operations under 5,000 dollars in sales are exempt.

verdicts.note: Higher labour, lower yields, certification and separate supply chains raise costs, but retail markups on organic often exceed the cost gap.
AAP clinical report (abstract only): despite the price premium, well-designed farming studies show organic costs can be competitive with conventional.

ERS says organic premiums rest on both higher production and handling costs and consumers' higher willingness to pay, sustained by label-enforced differentiation, and that premium levels vary by product and cannot be explained by a single set of factors; costs are a cause but not shown to be the main one.
